promptEn: An 8-second animated clip teaching the Traditional Chinese character 蛙 (frog). Lead: a round barrel-bodied toy pirate with a wooden peg leg and a grumpy blue-and-yellow parrot that turns its back on every command. Moment 1 (0-1.6s): the pirate scans with a telescope; the voice says 蛙 as a green stroke peeks in from the left edge and ducks away. Moment 2 (1.6-3.3s): strokes pop in from the top and right, dodging his net; the parrot points the wrong way; at the second 蛙 the pieces tiptoe to the center and settle into 蛙. Moment 3 (3.3-5s): a lily pad slides in; a bright green frog leaps out of the puddle at the pirate's feet and lands on his hat as the voice says 青蛙, his telescope popping off in surprise. Moment 4 (5-8s): glyph still; the frog rides the hat, the parrot finally smiles and flaps. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly "蛙、蛙、青蛙" (ㄨㄚ、ㄨㄚ、ㄑㄧㄥ ㄨㄚ), slowly and distinctly with clear tones, then stops; no other speech, no music louder than the voice. The only on-screen text is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 蛙, drawn as saturated solid leaf green strokes on a soft lemon yellow background, correctly formed, centered, filling about 70% of frame height with margins, perfectly still for the final 3-second hold while the lead keeps a small joyful motion away from the strokes. No vocabulary text, subtitles, watermark, clutter, flashing, real people or realistic humans; bright but not neon, no dark grading.
